note.question: How do information asymmetry, dual sourcing and supply market efficiency interact?
note.overview: The model considers opportunities for cooperation at the supply level between two firms that are rivals in the end-product market. One of our firms is vertically integrated (VI), has in-house production capabilities, and may also supply its rival. The other is a downstream outsourcing (DO) firm that has better market information.

source.quote: Problem definition: We consider opportunities for cooperation at the supply level between two firms that are rivals in the end-product market.
In their work, the buyer has demand information only for their ﬁrm, and not overall market demand information.
First of all, Arya et al. (2014) highlight the ﬁrst-mover advantage of placing an order to the rival as a major driver for the buyer to have the supply partnership.
The DO ﬁrm orders more under high demand and less under low demand.
However, there exists demand information asymmetry between the ﬁrms.

inputs.value: The efficiency of the outside supply market

source.quote: However, for low demand uncertainty, the VI’s wholesale price depends on the efﬁciency of the outside supply market.

inputs.value: Such diversification practices in a co-opetitive supply partnership

source.quote: We often observe such diversiﬁcation practices in a co-opetitive supply partnership.
Anticipating that, the VI may offer wholesale price concessions as an information rent to obtain the DO’s information.
Our work identifies demand uncertainty and efficiency of outside supply market as the factors affecting the VI’s pricing decision and the resulting equilibrium.
Given the wholesale price, the DO makes his ordering decision to the VI
